page: Hetzner Cloud cax41 is an Arm-based instance type in the Cost Optimized family, provisioned through the QEMU hypervisor. The server features 16 vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores of an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, configured with one thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. Memory capacity is set to 31.0 GB, which corresponds to 1.95 GB of RAM per core and reflects an approximate 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Local persistent storage is bundled with 320 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. The instance includes no discrete graphics hardware and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate balanced multi-threaded compute and I/O throughput offset by modest single-threaded metrics. The instance records a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,500.0 and a stress-ng multi-core rating of 29,117.84, both placing in the mid-range tier. In practical application tests, the system achieves 15,304.0 points in Clang compilation, 22.71 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations, and 16.72 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Conversely, single-threaded tasks show clear constraints: Geekbench single-core yields 1,052.0, single-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 7.08 GB/sec in the lower percentile, and PassMark memory performance scores 1,828.1.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the Ampere Altra architecture provides high core density per resource unit compared to traditional x86 allocations. The shared core model reduces overhead for horizontal concurrency but introduces variability under sustained per-core peak utilization. The platform is best suited for parallelized software compilation, containerized web applications, horizontal microservice clusters, and caching layers where high core counts take precedence over extreme single-threaded clock speed.
description: Hetzner Cloud cax41 is an Arm-based virtual server within the Cost Optimized family, powered by a 16-core Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz under a shared CPU allocation model. It is configured with 31.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 compute-to-RAM ratio, and includes 320 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Synthetic benchmarks reveal solid multi-core execution, demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,500.0, Clang software compilation at 15,304.0, and Redis throughput of 22.71 million operations per second. However, single-threaded throughput remains modest, with Geekbench single-core and bzip3 decompression registering in lower benchmark tiers. The instance delivers high resource density for concurrent workloads while trading off high single-core frequency. It is suitable for parallel build environments, containerized microservices, distributed caching, and static web serving.
